findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Date Marking. (A) Refrigerated, READY-TO-EAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 5C (41F) or less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1.

Two gallons of milk in the walk in cooler were observed partially used and without a date marking. When an employee was asked they believed that the containers were opened a couple days prior. Education was conducted and dates added to the containers to correct. Ensure that all TCS foods are dated once opened and if they are not emptied within 24 hours.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated.
findings.citation_text:
3-202.15 Package Integrity. FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants.

Two cans are observed with significant dents in the observable seams. The PIC was shown and education conducted. The cans were separated from the other cans for discarded/credit. Ensure that all can containers are maintained in good condition or separated out to prevent Botolism.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

The blade of the can opener is observed with dry, accumulated filth. The PIC was shown and cleaned the blade during the inspection to correct. Education conducted. Ensure that all food contact equipment are maintained clean in the facility.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114(B) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11.

On arrival the dish machine would not register at effective levels of sanitizer in the solution. The PIC was shown and investigated the situation. It appeared as if the jug of concentrate had off-gassed. A new jug was supplied and the concentration worked its way back up to effective levels during this inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food separated and protected.
findings.comment: Inspector observed a bowl of chicken in the WIC to be stored over ground beef. Cross contamination does not appear to have occurred. Discussed with PIC, and PIC moved the chicken below the ground beef. Facility has a storage order handout posted on the outside of the WIC. Ensure that food is stored in the correct order to prevent cross-contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-302.11(A)(2) Packaged and Unpackaged Food - Separation, Packaging, and Segregation. (A) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by: (2) Except when combined as ingredients, separating types of raw animal FOODS from each other such as beef, FISH, lamb, pork, and POULTRY during storage, preparation, holding, and display by: (a) Using separate EQUIPMENT for each type, or (b) Arranging each type of FOOD in EQUIPMENT so that cross contamination of one type with another is prevented, and (c) Preparing each type of FOOD at different times or in separate areas.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: Inspector observed the containers holding seasonings on the cart are soiled. Change containers and clean regularly. Store all food in clean covered containers.

 (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: Inspector observed a ladle with visible soil to be put away as clean.  Ensure that all food contact surfaces are properly cleaned before they are stored. Ladles may need soaking. The ladle was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. The violation is considered corrected on site. Take time to evaluate utensils for cleanliness when putting them up. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observes the back splash of the woks to have grease accumulation. Clean these more regularly and maintain them clean. 

4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
Inspector observes the threshold of the walk in cooler to be damaged. Repair the area so that it is smoother, cleanable, and does not pose a trip hazard.

6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
At this inspection the inspector observed that more ready to eat items are lacking date marks than are marked. Take care to label cooked battered chicken and ready to eat foods with date marking. Date tags were added to the items during the inspection. The violation is considered corrected on site. 

3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf). (C) Combined portions of food shall retain the date marking of the earliest-prepared food (Pf). (D) Approved date marking systems (C). (E)  Does not apply to repacked from a bulk container (C). (F) Does not apply to shellstock (C).  (G) Exemptions: prepared deli salads prepared according to 21 CFR 110; hard cheeses (39% moisture); semi-soft cheeses (50% or less); cultured dairy products (yogurt, sour cream, buttermilk); preserved fish (pickled herring, dried/salted); dry, fermented sausages (pepperoni); and salt-cured products (prosciutto and parma).

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

Observed clean utensils stored with handles in the holding container and food surfaces exposed to potential touch and splash contamination. Store clean utensils properly protected by having handles up in dispenser.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

The following non food contact surfaces are observed to have visible soil accumulation:
1. Area behind woks
2. Table edge to the right of woks and left of grill top
3. Basin of mop sink
4. Front of walk in cooler and handles/fronts of all coolers
5. Light fixtures in the storage room by double back door.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: (A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing. 

Some areas where ceiling meets the wall and walls join in little used area of the kitchen/storage areas have dust accumulation. Clean these areas and put on the regular cleaning list so that they do not accumulate dust webs.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Facility does not have a CFPM on staff. Owner has taken the course and has attempted to take the exam 6 times. Each time the computer kicks him out. He is scheduled to take the exam tomorrow. If the system kicks him out again, he is going to take the exam with SCDPH. 
This violation has been a repeat for the last two inspection. The facility may be required to have an administrative hearing to discuss the reason(s) the violation has not been corrected.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

(REPEAT) Observed the CFPM to not have proof of licensure. Discussed with PIC. PIC is having issues with the company he took the course with in order to schedule examination. Ensure the exam is completed and proof of license is available at the next routine inspection. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 10/4/22.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Observed no paper towels at the bar hand sink upon Inspector attempting to wash hands. Bartender provided new paper towels. Ensure hand sinks are stocked so proper hand washing may occur (need to dry hands and utilize a barrier to turn off the faucets). Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.comment:
3-501.16: (A) (1) TCS FOOD shall be maintained at 135F or above. Roasts can be maintained at 130F or above. 

Observed the fried rice hot holding to have a surface temperature of 110F. Observed the cheese sauce hot holding to have a surface temperature of 125F. Discussed hot holding temperatures being 135F. PIC rapidly reheated the items to 165F on the grill line/wok line per Inspector’s request. Hot held items had not been on the hot holding units for very long (facility opens at 4 PM). Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

(REPEAT) Observed the food handler’s licenses to not be available at the facility. Ensure all staff obtains a food handler’s license within 30 days of employment. Ensure copies are left at the facility. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 10/4/22.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.comment:
2-102.12: (A) The PERSON IN CHARGE shall be a certified FOOD protection manager who has shown proficiency of required information through passing a test that is part of an ACCREDITED PROGRAM. 

Observed the owner/PIC to not have the certified food protection manager’s license renewed yet. Ensure the class is completed and copy of license is available at the next routine inspection. Discussed with PIC. PIC has taken online course, but has yet to complete the exam.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the dish machine to not be priming on its own. It took several times in order to get the dish machine to dispense any bleach. Several runs were conducted with test strips checking sanitization levels - 0 ppm. After PIC primed the machine several times, it registered 50 ppm. PIC is called MJ Kellner to have the dish machine serviced. The machine is working; however, the issue should be permanently rectified. Utilize test strips to check bleach concentration (available). Inspector will follow-up on 10/6/22 to verify MJ Kellner has come to the facility and serviced the dish machine.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed no food handler’s licenses for staff. Only one was available for a former employee. PIC and employee stated that licenses were available. Ensure copies in the public health binder. Ensure new hires complete food handler’s certification within 30 days of employment. Discussed with PIC.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed bar hand sink to have beer bottle caps, refuse, and discarded sliced lemons in the sink. Cease dumping drinks in the sink. Hand washing sink is for hand washing only. Discussed with PIC. Keep hand washing sink accessible at all times for employee use. COS.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.11: Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of 2 adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with a supply of hand cleaning liquid, powder, or bar soap. 

Observed no soap at the bar hand sink. Provide soap at all times for hand sinks. Discussed with PIC. Soap was provided for the hand sink. COS.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Observed improper storage order within the walk-in cooler. Raw chicken was above raw beef. Ensure proper storage order. Chicken should be at the bottom of the storage shelf to protect against cross contamination. Chicken was moved to the bottom shelf. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

(REPEAT) Observed sani bucket in the kitchen to be dead - 0 ppm of bleach. PIC remade the bucket. Bleach for food-contact surfaces was used - approved bleach type. COS. Ensure bleach buckets stay at 50 to 200 ppm. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 12/15/21.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed sani bucket in the kitchen to be dead - 0 ppm of bleach. PIC remade bucket. Bleach is for food-contact surfaces and approved. 200 ppm. COS. Mindful to ensure bleach stays within 50 to 200 ppm.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following nonfood-contact areas in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. Spray nozzle near the dish machine has accumulation of food debris/grime on the handle and on top of the nozzle.
2. Shelving above the rice hot holding near the cook line has accumulation of dust.
3. Food debris along the base of the reach-in freezer.
4. Minor amount of dust on walk-in cooler fans.

Ensure to clean nonfood-contact surfaces as needed. #1 and #4 are repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 8/5/21.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following places no longer smooth and easily cleanable (in need of re-caulking):
1. Women’s bathroom hand sink.
2. Hand sink in the kitchen.
3. 3 compartment sink.
4. Dish machine area.

Ensure re-caulking before next routine inspection. #1 and #3 are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 8/5/21.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

(REPEAT) Observed ice machine to have mold accumulation along the interior baffle. Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/12/20. Inspector will follow-up on 8/16/21.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

(REPEAT) Observed multiple stacks of plates at the prep cooler top to not be protected from cross contamination - invert so food- and lip-contact surfaces are not exposed. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspections on 3/12/20 and 12/5/19.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11: (A) EQUIPMENT shall be maintained in good repair. (B) EQUIPMENT components shall be kept intact, tight, and adjusted to manufacturer’s specifications. (C) Cutting or piercing parts of can opens shall be kept sharp to minimize metal fragmentation. 

(REPEAT) Observed gasket/seal of the walk-in cooler door to be damaged and coming off the door. Discussed replacing seal/gasket with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 3/12/20.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-602.13: NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following NonFOOD-contact areas to be in need of cleaning due to soil accumulation:
1. Spray nozzle of the 3 compartment sink has a large accumulation of debris and grime on top of the nozzle and the handle.
2. Fans of the walk-in cooler has accumulation of dust.
3. Metal rolling cart was observed to have food splash and debris.

#1 and 3 are repeat violations from the 3/12/20 and 12/5/19 inspections. #2 is a repeat violation from the last routine inspection on 3/12/20.

Ensure routine cleaning of the NonFOOD-contact surfaces - wash, rinse, sanitize.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following areas to be in a state of disrepair and no longer smooth and easily cleanable:
1. 3 compartment sink in need of re-caulking (coming away from sink and wall)
2. Hand sink at the women’s bathroom needs re-caulking
3. Part of the frame is missing from the men’s bathroom door.

#1 and #2 are repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 3/12/20. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.14  (P) Employee changed gloves without washing hands between tasks. Food employee must practice good hygiene by properly washing hands when changing tasks. Reference 2-301.14.

Observed employee to help inspector with hand sink with single-use gloves on. Employee returned to food service without changing gloves or washing hands after touching the hand sink faucets. Discussed proper glove use and hadn washing with food handler. Food handler disposed of gloves, properly washed hands, and donned new single-use gloves. COS.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11  (P) Ready-to-eat foods (vegetables) stored below raw shell eggs. Store ready-to-eat food items above raw shell eggs to protect from cross-contamination. Reference 3-302.11.

Observed ready-to-eat food items (vegetables) to be stored below raw shell eggs. Discussed storage order with employee. Discussed storing raw shell eggs below ready-to-eat foods with PIC. Provided storage order paperwork with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Food contact surface is soiled with dust, dirt, food residue and other debris. Wash, rinse, sanitize food-contact surfaces routinely. Reference 4-601.11(A

Observed walk-in cooler metal wire shelving to be soiled with food debris and dust. Observed interior of ice machine to have mold accumulation. Discussed routine cleaning of food contact surfaces with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 3/23/30.
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114  (P) Chlorine sanitizer at 100 ppm at 3 compartment sink. Provide 50ppm to 200ppm chlorine concentration. Reference 4-501.114.

Observed chlorine dish machine to have appropriate bleach concentration, 100 ppm; however, the machine states it should be a minimum of 120 degree F. Inspector's maximum registering thermometer noted 110 degrees F after multiple attempts. Discussed repairs with PIC. Inspector will follow-up on 3/18/20.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on multiple food items within walk-in cooler. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed milk, fries, bacon, and noodles within walk-in cooler to lack date marking. Discussed appropriate date marking technique with PIC. Provided date marking paperwork with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspeciton on 12/5/19. COS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination. Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

Observed multiple areas where food utensils and plates were not protected from cross-contamination: plates on top of prep cooler, bowls on top of microwave, and clean forks/spoons above dish machine. Clean utensils and single-service articles should be kept in a manner that allows for food- and lip-contact surfaces to be protected such as flipped over. Forks and spoons should be stored in a manner that allows employees to reach for the non-food contact end of the utensil. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat violations since the last routine inspection on 12/5/20.
findings.citation_text:
4-901.11  (C) Equipment/Utensils are not properly Air-Dried after cleaning and sanitizing. After cleaning and sanitizing all equipment and utensils shall be air dried before use. Reference 4-901.11.

Observed multiple stacks of cups at bar area to have water within the cups and had not been properly air dried before stacking. Discussed ceasing practice with PIC.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment:
4-501.11 (C) Gaskets on the cooler door is cracked or missing. Replace the damaged or missing gaskets so the cooler can hold food at the proper temperature. Reference 4-501.11.

Observed gasket/seal of walk-in cooler door to be damaged. Discussed replacing with PIC.
findings.citation_text:
4-101.19  (C) Nonfood-contact surfaces of reach-in freezer is no longer easily cleanable. Reference 4-101.19.

Observed reach-in freezer to have accumulation of frost. Discussed routine cleaning of nonfood-contact surfaces with PIC.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-303.11 Cleaning Agents and Sanitizers, Availability
(A) Cleaning agents that are used to clean EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS as specified under Part 4-6, shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

Employee did not have sanitizer immediately available during prep.  Provide sanitation bucket at all times during preparation. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on various nonfood-contact surfaces. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed multiple areas of facility to have soil residue present on nonfood-contact surfaces:
1. (REPEAT) Spray nozzle of 3 compartment sink observed to have debris. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 12/5/19.
2. (REPEAT) Fans above hood observed to have large accumulation of dust. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 12/5/19.
3. Fans of walk-in cooler observed to have dust accumulation.
4. (REPEAT) Rolling cart for sauces observed to have heavy food debris and dust on metal shelving. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 12/5/19.
5. Door handles of reach-in freezer and ice machine observed to have debris and grime.

Discussed routine cleaning of nonfood-contact surfaces with PIC.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12 (A & B) (C) Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. Except for cleaning up a spill or other accident, cleaning should be done during periods when the least amount of food is exposed such as after closing.  Reference 6-501.12 (A & B).

Observed several areas of the physical facility that need cleaning:
1. Walls behind the 3 compartment sink and dish machine observed to have large accumulation of grease.
2. Floors beneath dish machine and 3 compartment sink need cleaned.
3. Area near reach-in freezer needs floor cleaning.

Discussed physical facilities being maintained cleaned with PIC.
findings.citation_text:
6-201.11  (C) Several areas were found in a state of disrepair, or not to be smooth and easily cleanable. Except as specified in Section 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.  Reference 6-201.11.

Observed several areas found in a state of disrepair or no longer smooth and easily cleanable: caulking of 3 compartment sink and hand sink within kitchen, as well as hand sinks of customer bathrooms. Missing coving near the spray nozzle area of the 3 compartment sink. Discussed repairs with PIC.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec.. 3.07. Allergen awareness training.
(b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed facility to lack necessary allergen training. Discussed certification for all CFPM's with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 12/5/19.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11  (Pf) Food employee filled liquid bucket for food prep in the hand sink in the kitchen area. Hand washing sink must be used for handwashing only. Reference 5-205.11.

Observed PIC to fill liquid bucket for food prep within the hand sink in kitchen. Discussed with PIC to only utilize hand washing sink for hand washing. COS.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17  (Pf) Date marking is not on various items within walk-in cooler. Food shall be clearly marked, at the time the original container is opened in a food establishment and if the food is held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded, when held at a temperature of 41 deg F or less for a maximum of 7 days (not exceeding a manufacturer's use-by date). Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

Observed multiple items within walk-in cooler to lack date marking: milk, wontons, various Chinese sauces. Discussed with PIC to date mark all items and discard within 7 days. COS. This is a repeat violation for the 2019 inspection year.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12  (P) Toxic bleach used in a way that contaminates food service utensils. Toxic materials must be used so that they cannot contaminate food, equipment, utensils, linens or single-service articles.  Reference 7-202.12.

Observed bottle of bleach used for sanitization to be stored under prep table/next to food service utensils (plates, etc.). Discussed with PIC that all toxic substances must be stored away from food-related items and in a manner that does not cross-contaminate. COS.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-904.11  (C) Clean utensils are not protected from contamination at prep area and 3 compartment sink (above). Clean utensils and single-service articles shall be handled, displayed and dispensed so that food- and lip-contact surfaces are protected form contamination. Reference 4-904.11.

Observed multiple stacks of plates near prep table area to be facing right side up, as well as mixing bowls above the 3 compartment sink. Discussed need to turn plates and bowls upside down in order to hinder cross-contamination. PIC was in compliance.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13  (C) Soil residue present on multiple areas of facility. Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

Observed an accumulation of soil residue present on multiple areas of facility:
1. Spray nozzle at 3 compartment sink was observed to have a large build up of soil residue on top of nozzle.
2. Fans above hood fryer (blowing into prep area of kitchen) and within walk-in cooler observed with accumulation of dust.
3. Rolling cart holding sauces at wok was observed with large accumulation of greese and residue.
4. Interior base of double door freezer was observed to have food crumbs.

Discussed routine cleaning of areas with PIC. This is a repeat violation for the 2019 inspection year.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-305.11  (C) Employee clothing and personal items were found stored improperly. Food establishments shall A) Provide designated dressing rooms or dressing areas for employees that routinely change their clothes in the establishment; B) Provide lockers or other suitable facilities for the orderly storage of employees' clothing and other possessions. Reference 6-305.11.

Observed personal salsa jar on top of lidded food items within top prep cooler. Observed personal food mixed with facility food in the bottom prep cooler. Discussed creating personal storage area in a cooler with PIC. PIC was in compliance and moved items.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PA 100-0367 (C) All CFPMs at a high risk facility should have completed an ANSI accredited allergen awareness program. Currently this has not taken place. Hand out were given to the PIC and they were instructed to ensure that all CFPMs complete an accredited course prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-602.11 Can opener had chunky buildup on the blade. Can opener was cleaned and sanitized during the inspection. 
Equipment food contact surfaces and utensils used with time/temperature control for safety food shall be cleaned between uses, any time contamination may have occurred, and up to every 4hrs after continuous use. 
Utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be sanitized before use after cleaning.

Measuring spoon for seasonings at wok was soiled with buildup. Measuring spoon was set aside at 3 part sink to be cleaned and sanitized. 
Surface inside the lid of the prep cooler was soiled with general buildup. Clean the inner surface of the lid on the prep cooler daily/as needed. Sanitize the lid after cleaning. 
Surfaces of utensils and equipment contacting food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food shall be cleaned at any time when contamination may have occurred or at least every 24hrs. 

Nozzle of soda gun at the bar had mold inside the tip. Nozzle was taken to 3 part sink to be cleaned and sanitized. Equipment such as beverage dispensing nozzles and enclosed components of equipment shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.12 Dried food splash was observed on the ceiling inside the microwave.
The cavities and door seals of microwave ovens shall be cleaned at least every 24 hours by using the manufacturer's recommended cleaning procedure.

findings.title: Proper hot holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Rice in small warmer set aside to make fried rice had an internal temperature of 116F. The small portion of rice observed below 135F was just removed from the large cooker of rice within the hour that was observed holding product at 177F. The small warmer accidentally got turned off. Warmer was turned back on to begin heating the rice, which was going to be fried and then hot held. 
Except during preparation, cooking, or cooling, or when time is used as the public health control, cooked hot foods that require time/temperature control for safety shall be maintained at 135°F/above.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Pan of cooked pork in the walkin cooler was observed without a date mark. Owner stated the pork was cooked and frozen within the last couple days. The pork was just pulled to be thawed for use today. Date mark of 7/24 was placed on the pan, and staff were advised the pork needs to be served or discarded within 6 days counting today as day 1 of 6. 
Refrigerated, ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature 41ºF/less for a maximum of 7 days. The day of preparation shall be counted as Day 1. If products are frozen, then dates need to be changed and documented accordingly to reflect proper time frame for use and ensure the foods are used or discarded within a total of 7 days.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-204.11 Bleach without proper label was available for use. Employee went to store and purchased bleach with a proper label that had an EPA registration number and instructions for sanitizing food contact surfaces with a concentration listed in ppm. Bleach without proper label was set aside to be used for general cleaning and disinfecting purposes. 
Chemical sanitizers, including chemical sanitizing solutions generated on-site, and other chemical antimicrobials applied to food contact surfaces shall meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940 Tolerance exemptions for active and inert ingredients for use in antimicrobial formulations (Food-contact surface sanitizing solutions).

findings.title: Insects, rodents, and animals not present
findings.citation_text:
6-202.15 A half dozen flies were observed in the kitchen at the time of inspection. The back door was open in the kitchen, and the screen door was observed to not be tight fitting with gaps along edges and a tear in the screen. The screen door was also not properly attached to the door frame.
Repair the screen door so it is protected against the entry of pests.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Floors under and around equipment are in need of detail cleaning, especially in the storage area by the back door and the area where the chest freezer is located. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 Sec. 3.07 Certified food managers have not completed the online food allergen awareness training. Requirements for allergen training were discussed, and information was provided for management to find an online course.
All certified food managers need to complete the food allergen awareness training by the next routine inspection

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text: 2-301.12  (P) Food employee improperly washed hands. Handle was turned off with clean hands and not a barrier. Discussed with operator.  Food employees shall properly wash their hands and exposed portion of their arms for at least 20 seconds, with approved soap and drying methods, according to this section of the food code. Reference 2-301.12.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text: 7-204.11  (P) Available bleach is not approved for use as a sanitizer. Bleach should be EPA registered with food contact sanitizing instructions present on label (should read as a ppm). Chemical sanitizers must meet the requirements specified in 40 CFR 180.940, or meet the requirements as specified in 40 CFR 180.2020. Reference 7-204.11.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text: 4-602.13  (C) Observed the following non-food contact surfaces to be soiled: 1) rolling cart holding sauces at wok (grease and food splash); 2) interior base and vent of prep cooler (grease); and 3) interior base of double door freezer (food crumbs). Clean all non-food contact surfaces frequently to prevent soil accumulation.  Reference 4-602.13.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: Certified food managers do not have allergen training certificates. Provide certificates by next routine inspection.
